πομπ-εία , ἡ,
A.leading in procession, solemn procession,
Plb. 30.25.2 .
II. abuse, ribaldry, such as was allowed to those who took part in the processions at the festivals of Dionysus and Demeter, D. 18.11 , Men. Per.Fr. 4 (pl.): metaph., ἡ τοῦ δαίμονος καθ᾽ ἡμῶν π. the mock that fate makes of us,
Hld. 5.6 , cf. Philostr. VS 2.27 .
From A Greek-English Lexicon (Henry George Liddell, Robert Scott, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1940)
